**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute calculated rates for manual lookup results**

When a user is already on the Calculate rate tab and changes the date to one for which the lookup returns `Exchange rate not found`, this branch clears the hidden exchange-rate input even though the source and destination amounts—and the displayed calculated rate—remain. The successful-response path above explicitly calls `calculateRateFromAmounts()` for this tab, but the manual-rate path does not, so submitting the transfer omits the custom rate and repeats the failed server lookup. Recalculate from the typed amounts here instead of blanking the field when `activeTab === "calculateRate"`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Keep the restored rate when the initial lookup fails.** If the initial fetch rejects or returns invalid JSON, `fetchExchangeRate` calls `hideExchangeRateField`. This clears the restored rate and hides its input, despite an unchanged currency pair and date. Successful responses preserve that same rate. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/we-promise/sure/6a524b0353e4bd9a8c52437cb14a9145b84f218c/app/javascript/controllers/exchange_rate_form_controller.js)) For this failure path, retain the rendered rate and show manual entry. Continue clearing the rate when currencies are missing or equal. This completes the rejected-submit preservation behavior described in the PR objectives.

Preserve clearing behavior when currencies are missing or equal. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Do not discard valid cents in the unrounded submission path.** For `12345678901234.25`, this computes one decimal place and returns `12345678901234.3`. `toFixed(1)` rounds the value; this is not float-drift removal. ([tc39.es](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/numbers-and-dates.html?utm_source=openai)) The value is within the supported amount bound. When a currency lookup is pending, the money-field controller uses this formatter for submission, so the amount changes by `0.05`. The previous ten-decimal formatting retained `.25`. Preserve meaningful input digits instead of applying a global 15-significant-digit limit. Keep the existing tiny-rate and float-drift cases working. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/we-promise/sure/6a524b0353e4bd9a8c52437cb14a9145b84f218c/app/javascript/utils/evaluate_amount_expression.js))

Keep the existing tiny-rate and float-drift handling working. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Correct the invalid-amount message: zero fees are valid.** `Transfer::Creator` rejects only negative fees. A zero fee is treated as no fee, and the transfer is created. The `amounts_invalid` error is raised for a zero or negative exchange rate and for a negative fee. When the rate is zero and both fees are zero, the user can fix the submission by changing only the rate. The message still says that the fees must be positive. Users may then enter fees they did not pay. State the actual rules in the message. The exchange rate must be positive, and fees must not be negative. Apply the change to the English source key and to every locale that defines `transfers.create.amounts_invalid`. The same wording appears in all `config/locales/views/transfers/*.yml` files, so changing only `nl.yml` leaves the defect in the other files.
